item.title: From Risk Reduction to a Digital Platform: How We Localized CRM at AstraZeneca, Russia and Eurasia
item.description:
In 2022, our team had a specific task: to prepare a local replacement for the global CRM so that employees could continue their usual work without interruption. The system was already part of daily processes. It was used to plan visits to healthcare professionals, record interaction results, and manage communications. The main driver for localization was the risk of the global solution being disconnected. But there were other reasons too: the desire for more flexibility in system development, simplification of certain processes, and consolidation of several existing local solutions into a single platform. At the time, no one was thinking about a digital assistant, artificial intelligence, automatic visit planning, or migrating other corporate systems into the CRM. The primary goal was to maintain business continuity and gain control over the platform's future development. Several years later, it became clear that the outcome was far more ambitious than initially conceived. Read more

item.title: How to Tame the LLM Dragon. Corporate AI Gateway Architecture and Limitations of Classic Proxies in Working with Neural Networks
item.description:
The first step in the spontaneous adoption of neural networks is to block direct external access and route requests through the familiar corporate proxy. However, generative AI has its own specifics: standard proxies cannot detect sensitive data in model responses, don't see prompt leaks, and don't protect against token overspending. Below is the first part of a series on building a corporate AI gateway: why classic load balancers are not designed for LLMs, how a specialized architecture works, and how the AI Optimum platform provides context control, transparent token accounting, and data security.

item.title: AnythingLLM: Chat with Your Documents Without an OpenAI Subscription
item.description:
Imagine having a folder full of contracts, a hundred PDFs, notes, and internal documentation on your disk. You open ChatGPT, upload one file – it reads it. Upload more, and the context overflows, or the file gets lost. What if you have ten files? Twenty? A subscription costs money, requires a VPN from Russia, and even then, the model doesn't know what's in your spreadsheets unless you feed it everything manually. This is where AnythingLLM comes in – an open-source application that turns your files into a knowledge base and lets you chat with them using any LLM. Want it local and free on your graphics card? Done. Want to use a cloud model without an OpenAI subscription and hassle? That's also an option, and we'll walk through it step-by-step below. This article is about how to set up a private assistant in an evening that can answer questions based on your documents. With blackjack and RAG!

item.title: Which LLM Will Make a Good Virtual Employee, or Why Code Generation Model Benchmarks Are Failing
item.description:
In February 2026, OpenAI recommended the SWE-Bench Pro benchmark for evaluating AI programming agents. However, by July 8, they retracted their recommendation, admitting that approximately 30% of SWE-Bench Pro tasks contain errors. Previously, the company abandoned SWE-bench Verified when it was discovered that models had seen parts of its tasks and solutions during training. This raises the question: which tests can be trusted at all? While the industry grapples with this, NVIDIA researchers have tackled another issue, particularly relevant for developers of code generation models and those building AI agents based on them. Read on.

item.title: Finally, I Understood Andrey Karpatsky with the Help of Arkanoid
item.description:
This is the last frame of DOS Arkanoid from 1988. The VAUS ship flies away because the boss DOH was defeated in round 33. The game has no API, meaning no ready-made programmatic entry, and no one hacks into its memory. There's only a 320x200 pixel image, a keyboard, and a mouse. Before this frame, a program written by AI reached this point in 10 out of 10 games. The AI itself didn't play. It studied the game by looking at the screen and wrote a regular player program, which then played. Claude and I prepared access to the game and a separate verification program together, and I set the tasks. Six months ago, in April 2026, I watched Andrey Karpatsky's presentation at the Sequoia AI Ascent conference (there's also a Russian dub). He talked about three generations of software. In Software 1.0, humans write code. In Software 2.0, you collect data and train a neural network. In Software 3.0, 'programming turns into prompting,' and what's in the context window becomes 'the lever with which you control the interpreter, i.e., the LLM.' I watched, nodded, and, as I understand now, understood nothing. I am not a professional programmer. Words about vibe-coding, agents, and the new paradigm have long become an abstraction for me: they sound smart, but you can't touch them. Recently, I rewatched that presentation and was surprised that I now understand almost every word. Over these six months, I've recognized my own experience in his words. First, I tried to teach AI to play Arkanoid by training a neural network, and I failed. Then I set the task differently, and it worked. This article is about that: how a simple 1988 game explained to me what a lecture couldn't. Read more

item.title: How to Conduct Technical Interviews in the Era of AI-Powered Scribes and Agent Development
item.description:
Standard technical screening and classic live coding are rapidly losing their meaning: during online interviews, candidates widely use invisible AI scribes (like Ghost GPT), and any modern LLM can solve typical algorithmic problems in seconds. Trying to combat this with prohibitions and proctoring is a dead end. At SymbioWay, we decided to take an opposite approach: we officially allowed candidates to use AI agents directly in interviews, but changed the tasks themselves so that the neural network couldn't help without a deep understanding of architecture and code. In this article, I'll explain what skills we now test in developers and how these tasks are structured.

item.title: Millions of lines or millions of parameters: how we found the balance for kazRush — an open-source Russian-Kazakh translation model
item.description:
In the task of training a machine translation model, there's a pleasant moment: you find several million sentence pairs and for a second, you feel like the hardest part is over. Then you open a random line. On the left is a sentence, on the right is a table fragment. The next pair has the same topic, but not the meaning. A bit further, someone carefully put HTML remnants into the text. The dataset arrived with the furniture of previous tenants. For low-resource languages, this is compounded by the limited availability of parallel data. Therefore, it's especially useful here to understand what exactly the model receives as input and what architecture we are trying to train on it. This is Anya Lebedeva, a developer in the AI VK experimental technologies department, and today I will talk about kazRush — a system for translating from Russian to Kazakh and back. We collected and cleaned a corpus from open sources, trained models from scratch, and selected a model configuration with approximately 197 million parameters. Along the way, it turned out that stricter cleaning sometimes worsens the result, a larger vocabulary is not necessarily more useful, and increasing the model to 738 million parameters does not solve the problem by itself. In general, several quite reasonable ideas had to be sent back to the door, but the final result justified the effort. The Russian-Kazakh model took first place in its track at LoResMT 2026 — a workshop at the EACL conference. Read more

item.title: Kodacode 1.3: The agent can now interact with applications and has its own browser
item.description:
Kodacode 1.3 has been released, enabling interaction with computer applications. The Desktop version now includes a built-in browser for viewing web pages alongside the chat and easily sharing content with the agent. Additionally, the update introduces change previews without Git, interactive prototypes, AI agent automation flows, and an improved CLI for CI integration. This article details these new features, including a look at the new pet.
